item.title: 32nd Annual Hoike Hula Concert Saturday
item.description: LIHUE — Na Hoku Hanohano Award winner and Grammy nominee Kumu Hula Leilani Rivera Low and her Halau Hula O Leilani will celebrate the 32nd annual Ho‘ike Hula Concert on Saturday at the Kauai War Memorial Convention Hall.

item.title: Hawaiian Home Lands rent-to-own prospect has few takers
item.description: The state Department of Hawaiian Home Lands hasn’t convinced many beneficiaries to take a new path to homeownership at a unique rent-to-own project despite more than $1 million in touted benefits.

item.title: EDITORIAL: Unmask federal agents in Hawaii
item.description: Masks have been on Americans’ minds — and faces — for the better part of a decade, in 2019 as welcome protection during the pandemic (or unnecessary ideological totem, according to those of a particular political bent), but more recently as a symbol of calculated obfuscation. item.title: KPD Commends officers for exceptional service and leadership
item.description: LIHUE — The Kauai Police Department (KPD) recognized Sgt. Brian Silva and Officer Joridan Sele as the Employees of the Month for February, honoring their exceptional dedication, professionalism and commitment to public safety.

item.title: Red Hill: Fears linger over Navy reopening water shaft
item.description: After waiting hours to hear the latest update on the Red Hill water crisis cleanup at a lengthy meeting Tuesday with the Commission on Water Resource Management, concerned community members learned the Navy had left the meeting.

item.title: St. Theresa School seeking support for carnival fundraiser
item.description: KEKAHA — The St. Theresa School Carnival is coming to the school’s Kekaha campus on April 18 announced St. Theresa School Principal Wendy Souza.

item.title: Hawaii Department of Transportation-Airports Division seeks input
item.description: LIHUE — More than a dozen people opted to spend their lunch hour with the Lihue Airport Optimization Plan team on Wednesday at the Moikeha Building Conference Rooms.

item.title: Hawaii bills would curb keiki phone use in schools, and for social media, AI
item.description: Hawaii’s keiki could soon face tighter limits on phone use at school, social media access and interactions with artificial intelligence under bills that continue to move through the Legislature.
